resources.string: Sapu Berita opens news links in a clean version: no ads, no \"Baca Juga\" link lists, and every page merged into one.
News links from WhatsApp, Telegram and other apps open clean.
Your browser stays as it is. Other links don\'t change.
No account, no server. Everything runs on your phone.
Let Sapu Berita open news links
Android needs your permission once. The button below opens a settings page like this:
It may look slightly different on your phone.
Tick all %2$d boxes (scroll down to see them all), then tap \"%1$s\".
No \"%1$s\" button? Look for \"%2$s\" on the page that opens.
Done! Active on all %1$d news sites.
Active on %1$d of %2$d sites. Not ticked yet: %3$s
Not active yet. Tap \"Open settings\" and follow the steps above.
\"%1$s\" is still off. Turn it on first, then add the links.
%1$s opens in the %2$s app, so it can\'t be picked here. That\'s fine; the other sites still work.
Pick Sapu Berita for news links
Tap the button below. Your phone asks which app to use:
Done! News links now open in Sapu Berita.
News links still always open in %1$s. Clear that first: on the page that opens, find \"%2$s\" and then \"%3$s\".
Open a sample Kompas article. Aa sets text size and theme; Asli shows the original page.
Instagram, Facebook and TikTok open links in their own browser. Choose \"Open in browser\" from the ⋮ menu.
Everything runs on your phone. Sapu Berita has no server and doesn\'t know what you read. Once a day it checks GitHub for a new version and site fixes (turn off under Aa → Cek update).
